pending_port.why: The sister has its OWN 378-line tv_throttle.py with a --wait design, not this one. It lacks the 100/min hard bound, the per-endpoint (scanner vs chart) lanes, the learned ceiling_rpm and the AIMD recovery. Its observed signal ('Rate limit exceeded. Retry after 32s') IS already handled by this repo's detect_limit, so the port is additive rather than a rewrite.

pending_port.summary: Weekly chart fallback once a run covers 3+ tickers (chart_data.py --interval)
pending_port.why: Material to the screener above all: it sweeps sector by sector, so EVERY run covers many tickers and hits the bars-per-ticker wall this fixes. A daily 200-period line needs ~500 bars per name; a weekly 40-period line ~190. Without it a multi-name run silently ships charts whose long-term average starts partway across.

pending_port.summary: relative_strength.py: ret_over tolerance, and dict-bar input
pending_port.why: Drift the OTHER way - this repo has it, the sister does not. ret_over here clamps to the oldest bar when the series is within 90% of the window (IBKR's ONE_YEAR returns ~251 bars for a 252-session lookback); the sister returns None, so the same data yields a 12-month RS here and a blank there. That is a computed number differing between the skills. as_row/normalize (accepting TradingView {t,o,h,l,c,v} dicts) is input-format only, not maths.
